editorial.thesis: A hospitality-and-food-and-drink city of about 161,000. Its retail is heavy on restaurants & fast food and desserts, sweets & ice cream, and thin on coaching & training and apparel, footwear & jewellery — and 35% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is ahead of Delhi. 52.17 chain outlets per lakh residents against 18.83 in Delhi; 25 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Baskin Robbins 14, Apollo Pharmacy 13, Domino's 11.

The mapped economy leans to hotels & stays. Shares of all mapped places: hotels & stays 11.7% (Delhi 4.4%); food & beverage 17.7% (Delhi 8.0%); offices 4.8% (Delhi 11.7%); education 3.9% (Delhi 7.9%). Raw counts would mislead because Delhi is mapped more completely (87,703 places against 4,305), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 4 zones hold 35% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Navelim alone has about 22,000 residents and 15 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is more concentrated than in Delhi. 53% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Delhi 47%). The largest cores are Gandhi Complex · Aquem (1,070 places) and Colva (290).

The widest brand gaps against Delhi. Café Coffee Day 6 outlets vs 145; Domino's 11 outlets vs 140; Apollo Pharmacy 13 outlets vs 108. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 5 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Delhi, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Gandhi Complex · Aquem and Navelim are the largest zones by residents (56,000 and 22,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 53% of all commercial places, and Gandhi Complex · Aquem alone lists 1,070.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Gandhi Complex · Aquem holds 43 of the 84 tracked chain outlets, and Colva adds 6.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Gandhi Complex · Aquem and Fatorda lead on education places (75 and 11, with 24 and 3 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Navelim and Benaulim. The blue cores include Gandhi Complex · Aquem.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (87,703 places in Delhi against 4,305 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Delhi; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Delhi, Margao's mapped places over-index on hotels & stays (11.7% vs 4.4%), food & beverage (17.7% vs 8.0%), desserts & sweets (1.3% vs 0.7%) and under-index on offices (4.8% vs 11.7%), education (3.9% vs 7.9%), other services (5.3% vs 8.9%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 84 outlets of 25 tracked national brands within 5 km — 52.17 per lakh residents against Delhi's 18.83 (1289 outlets of 45 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Delhi are Café Coffee Day (6 vs 145); Domino's (11 vs 140); Apollo Pharmacy (13 vs 108). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Delhi's, so low means thin by Delhi's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 5 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Margao's age mix against Delhi: children (0–14) 21.1% vs 23.1%, 15–24 17.1% vs 20.4%, working age 50.8% vs 49.7%, 60+ 10.9% vs 6.8%. Under-25s are 38% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 13.5% of mapped places against 5.7% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 11 (Delhi 140), KFC 6 (Delhi 51), Pizza Hut 6 (Delhi 68), Wow! Momo 2 (Delhi 32).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 3.5% of mapped places against 2.1% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 6 (Delhi 145), Starbucks 1 (Delhi 33). No mapped outlet in either city: Chai Sutta Bar.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.4% of mapped places against 0.7% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 14 (Delhi 29), Naturals 1 (Delhi 7). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 3.9% of mapped places against 2.2% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: DMart 1 (Delhi 7), Big Bazaar 1 (Delhi 8), Vishal Mega Mart 1 (Delhi 11). No mapped outlet in either city: Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.7% of mapped places against 1.2% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 13 (Delhi 108), Wellness Forever 1 (Delhi 0). No mapped outlet in either city: MedPlus, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 5.1% of mapped places against 7.0% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 5 (Delhi 66), Westside 3 (Delhi 15), Titan 3 (Delhi 21), Pantaloons 1 (Delhi 8).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 6.7% of mapped places against 7.9% in Delhi — below its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 0.8% of mapped places against 2.7% in Delhi — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 3.0% of mapped places against 3.9% in Delhi — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
